threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is a 'nice' area instead of just a spot to change trains and avoid the real action.
Caught a guy singing opera on the 133 last night. Had the whole upper deck in stitches. Never thought I'd find a night bus serenade so entertaining.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw an old lady in the Kiez, knitting a scarf while casually critiquing the latest BVG strike. Only in Neukölln do protests blend with cozy afternoons.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do they hold spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings. You never know when you'll stumble upon a rave while walking home.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know which burrito joint has the best poached egg special—tourists still ask for extra guac.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy wrestling with a dog on the Civic Center tracks while the bus was packed. Only in San Francisco could chaos have a side of comedy.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals drink 'cava' at brunch; most of us prefer a 'café amb llet' and a croissant from the bakery on the corner.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their over-reliance on Google Maps for walking routes; locals know shortcuts through the narrow streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 bus runs on time. Everyone here knows it’s just a guideline, not an actual schedule.
Caught a whiff of fried plantain on the 59 last night. Two guys debating the best jollof recipes—very Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a pigeon steal a döner right off a tourist’s plate at Hermannplatz. You don’t get that in any brochure.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, the kebab shops have names like 'Rosa' and 'Dönerteller Express' that use neon lights to turn a late-night bite into a mini disco.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for tourists blocking the sidewalk at Valencia and 24th while fumbling with their cameras.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I watched a street performer juggle while Muni was stalled for 20 minutes. Only in the Tenderloin do you find live art during a transit meltdown.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every building with a Gaudí façade is a museum. Many locals just see it as another overpriced restaurant waiting to happen.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they take a selfie next to every street sign, thinking the grungy graffiti is part of the 'authentic' experience.
